notes: This source (12 CFR Part 1266, FHFA Advances regulation) governs Federal Home Loan Bank advances to members and housing associates — collateral, pricing, fees, terms, secured-creditor priority, and related operational rules for FHLB advances. The ratified scope for this Phase 2 distillation is limited to a diagnostic of the current U.S. bank liquidity regime as it pertains to fast-moving bank runs, specifically: (1) fragmentation/lack of interoperability between Federal Reserve discount-window and FHLB collateral/operational rules; (2) structural sources of discount-window stigma; (3) timing/granularity defects in liquidity reporting instruments (Call Reports, FR 2052a, etc.) contributing to slow detection/response; (4) a defect register; and (5) mapping of reform proposals (e.g., Hsu, McKernan) against those defects. The source text provided is the standalone FHFA Advances regulation itself — definitions of Advance, collateral categories, pricing, fees, member eligibility, housing associate advances, etc. — and contains no discussion, comparison, or cross-reference to Federal Reserve discount-window rules, no discussion of discount-window stigma, no discussion of Call Report or FR 2052a timing/granularity, and no discussion of any reform proposals by Acting Comptroller Hsu or Undersecretary McKernan. While the regulation is plausibly *background material* relevant to the broader program topic (FHLB collateral practices are one side of the fragmentation problem the ratified scope asks about), the ratified scope requires extraction of the diagnostic content ITSELF (the mapping/cataloguing/defect analysis), not raw source rules from which such a diagnostic might later be constructed by a separate analytical process. Nothing in this source text as given constitutes or states such a diagnostic, defect register, or reform-mapping; it is purely the operative text of the advances regulation. Per the instruction to extract ONLY content within the ratified scope, and per the fidelity rule against inventing analysis not present in the source, this item is marked nothing_in_scope: true, with no obligations/definitions/interactions extracted, notwithstanding that the underlying regulation may serve as a citable input to a later-stage comparative analysis conducted elsewhere in the program.
